mainTopic: The weights of the crimson wool strips (לשון של זהורית) used for the פרה אדומה, the שעיר המשתלח, and the מצורע, and רבי יצחק's doubt about which שחיטה may be done by a זר: the פרה אדומה or the פר of the כהן גדול.
overview: This amud opens by finishing a ruling about the weight of the crimson strip used for the פרה אדומה, the שעיר המשתלח and the מצורע. רבי יוחנן reports a מחלוקת about the פרה's strip. רבי ירמיה מדיפתי says the dispute was really about the שעיר's strip, and the death of רביא בר קיסי that day became its סימן. Next, רבי יצחק remembers that a זר may slaughter either the פרה or the פר of the כהן גדול, but he does not remember which one. רב and שמואל disagree about this, and the גמרא proves that רב is the one who invalidates the פרה, because of the words ״אלעזר״ and ״חוקה״. The גמרא defends רב with several points: שחיטה is not an עבודה, the פרה is קדשי בדק הבית, and מראות נגעים show that a כהן can be required even where there is no עבודה. For שמואל, the verse ״לפניו״ shows that a זר slaughters while אלעזר watches. The גמרא then explains the rule against taking one's attention off the פרה, and why it must be written for both slaughtering and burning. The amud ends as the גמרא begins asking which stage this rule leaves out, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The weight of each crimson strip
steps.stepSummary: The ruling from the previous daf continues: the crimson strip of the פרה weighs ten זוז, the strip of the שעיר המשתלח weighs two סלעים, and the strip of the מצורע weighs one שקל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The crimson strip of the פרה weighs ten זוז. The strip of the שעיר המשתלח weighs two סלעים. The strip of the מצורע weighs one שקל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a ruling that started on the previous daf. It lists how heavy the crimson strip must be for three different rituals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three rituals and three different weights. A סלע equals four זוז, so two סלעים is eight זוז. A שקל equals two זוז. The weights therefore go down in order: ten for the פרה, eight for the שעיר, and two for the מצורע.

keyTerms.meaning: The red heifer (פרה אדומה), whose ashes purify from contact with the dead
The goat sent away to עזאזל on יום כיפור
A person with צרעת who brings a purification offering
A coin and weight unit; a סלע equals four זוז
Plural of סלע, a coin worth four זוז

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the start of a new topic. The ruling began on the previous daf, and This amud opens in the middle of it.

phrases.english: The strip of the red heifer: the weight of ten zuz,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁל שָׂעִיר הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ — מִשְׁקַל שְׁנֵי סְלָעִים,
phrases.english: and that of the scapegoat: the weight of two sela'im (eight zuz),
and that of the leper: the weight of a shekel (two zuz).
phrases.notes: Here a שקל equals two זוז.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ruling begun on the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Crimson strip weights: פרה is ten זוז, שעיר המשתלח is two סלעים, מצורע is one שקל.

steps.title: A dispute over the weight of the heifer's strip
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reports that רבי שמעון בן חלפתא and the רבנן disagree about the פרה's strip. One says ten זוז and the other says one שקל. He gives the סימן "אחד המרבה ואחד הממעיט".
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: רבי שמעון בן חלפתא and the רבנן disagree about the פרה's strip. One says it weighs ten זוז, and one says it weighs a שקל. Your memory aid: "Both the one who gives much and the one who gives little."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds that the weight of the פרה's strip is actually disputed. He gives a short phrase to help us remember the two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 gave ten זוז as if it were settled. Now we learn it is only one side of a מחלוקת, and the other side says just one שקל. The סימן "the one who gives much and the one who gives little" reminds us that the two opinions are the extremes: the largest amount (ten) and the smallest (a שקל). Nobody picks the middle amount of two סלעים.

keyTerms.meaning: They disagree
Your mnemonic, a memory aid
"Both the one who does much and the one who does little", a phrase borrowed from a משנה

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן חֲלַפְתָּא וְרַבָּנַן בְּפָרָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Chalafta and the Rabbis disagree about it, regarding the heifer's strip:
one says: the weight of ten zuz;
and one says: the weight of a shekel.
And your mnemonic: "Both the one who gives much and the one who gives little."
phrases.notes: The two views are the two extremes: the most (ten) and the least (a שקל).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן חֲלַפְתָּא וְרַבָּנַן בְּפָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the weight of the פרה's strip from Step 1 is actually disputed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת about the פרה's strip: ten זוז versus one שקל.

steps.title: The dispute was really about the scapegoat
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה מדיפתי tells רבינא that the disagreement was not about the פרה's strip but about the strip of the שעיר המשתלח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה מדיפתי said to רבינא: They do not disagree about the פרה. Rather, they disagree about the שעיר המשתלח.
steps.whatsHappening: A later אמורא corrects the report of the מחלוקת. He says it belongs to a different ritual.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's version placed the dispute on the פרה. רבי ירמיה מדיפתי moves it to the שעיר המשתלח. On this version, the weight of the פרה's strip (ten זוז) is agreed by everyone, and only the שעיר's strip is in question.

keyTerms.meaning: "Not... but rather", the formula used to correct a claim

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מִדִּיפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya of Difti said to Ravina:
They do not disagree about the heifer's strip,
rather, they disagree about the scapegoat's strip.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא בְּפָרָה פְּלִיגִי, אֶלָּא בְּשָׂעִיר הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects which ritual the dispute in Step 2 is about.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the claim that the dispute concerns the פרה. It does not reject the existence of the dispute.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The dispute was reported under the wrong ritual.

steps.title: A sage's death becomes the memory aid
steps.stepSummary: On the day this dispute was discussed, רביא בר קיסי died. The sages made his death the סימן: "רביא בר קיסי atones like the שעיר המשתלח."
steps.simpleTranslation: And on that day רביא בר קיסי died, and they made a סימן from it: רביא בר קיסי atones like the שעיר המשתלח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story to explain how the sages remembered that the dispute was about the שעיר המשתלח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The death of a צדיק brings כפרה for his generation, just as the שעיר המשתלח brings כפרה. The sages linked רביא בר קיסי's death to the שעיר. That link fixed in memory that the dispute was about the שעיר and not the פרה, which matches רבי ירמיה מדיפתי's version.

keyTerms.meaning: His soul rested; he died
A sage who died on that day
A mnemonic sign
Atones

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of the מחלוקת about the weight of a crimson strip. רבי יוחנן says it concerns the פרה, and רבי ירמיה מדיפתי says it concerns the שעיר המשתלח. Each version has its own סימן.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָהוּא יוֹמָא נָח נַפְשֵׁיהּ דְּרַבְיָא בַּר קִיסִי,
phrases.english: And on that day Ravya bar Kisi died,
and they set a mnemonic in it:
Ravya bar Kisi atones like the scapegoat.
phrases.notes: The death of a צדיק atones for his generation.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָהוּא יוֹמָא נָח נַפְשֵׁיהּ דְּרַבְיָא בַּר קִיסִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the memory aid that anchors רבי ירמיה מדיפתי's version.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The סימן linking the dispute to the שעיר המשתלח is the death of רביא בר קיסי, which atones like the שעיר.

steps.title: רבי יצחק's forgotten tradition about slaughter by a non-כהן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק heard that of two slaughterings, the פרה אדומה and the פר of the כהן גדול, one is valid when done by a זר and the other is invalid. He does not remember which is which.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: I heard about two slaughterings, one of the פרה אדומה and one of his bull (the פר of the כהן גדול). One is valid when done by a זר and one is invalid when done by a זר, but I do not know which of them is which.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבי יצחק presents a tradition he only half remembers, and this sets up the discussion that follows, where the גמרא will try to figure out which slaughtering is which.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually שחיטה does not need a כהן. Even for קדשים, a זר may slaughter. רבי יצחק knows that one of these two special slaughterings breaks that pattern, but he has forgotten which one. The doubt is real, and it opens a new line of inquiry.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughterings
"His bull": the פר of the כהן גדול on יום כיפור
A non-כהן
Valid / invalid
I do not know

steps.confusionAlert: פָּרָה (the red heifer) and פָּרוֹ (his bull, meaning the כהן גדול's bull) look almost the same. Read carefully: they are two different animals.
steps.whyThisMatters: It raises a basic question: does a slaughtering that must be done by the כהן גדול himself, or a non-altar offering like the פרה, require a כהן for the שחיטה?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
I heard a teaching about two slaughterings:

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל פָּרָה, וְאַחַת שֶׁל פָּרוֹ.
phrases.english: one of the red heifer, and one of his (the High Priest's) bull.
One is valid when done by a non-priest,
and one is invalid when done by a non-priest,
but I do not know which of them is which.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: שְׁתֵּי שְׁחִיטוֹת שָׁמַעְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: whether a זר may slaughter the פרה or the פר of the כהן גדול.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One of the two (פרה or פרו of the כהן גדול) may be slaughtered by a זר and the other may not. רבי יצחק does not know which is which. Step 6 shows that this is a dispute between רב and שמואל, and step 7 identifies רב's side.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which slaughtering is valid by a זר: the פרה אדומה or the פר of the כהן גדול?

steps.title: רב and שמואל disagree about a non-כהן slaughtering the פרה and the פר
steps.stepSummary: An אמוראic dispute is reported. One of רב and שמואל says a זר makes the פרה invalid but the פר valid. The other says the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: about slaughtering the פרה and his bull (the כהן גדול's פר), רב and שמואל disagree. One said the פרה is invalid and his bull is valid. The other said his bull is invalid and the פרה is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an argument between רב and שמואל. It is the same question רבי יצחק was unsure about: which one may a non-כהן slaughter?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק heard that one of the two is valid with a זר and the other is not, but he forgot which. Here we learn this was a real dispute. רב and שמואל each take one side, but we are not yet told who holds which view.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtering an animal
"His bull": the פר the כהן גדול brings on יום כפור
A non-כהן

steps.confusionAlert: "פרו" does not mean "his cow." It means the כהן גדול's own bull on יום כפור. The word "פרה" here always means the פרה אדומה.

phrases.english: It was stated: the slaughter of the heifer and his bull,
phrases.notes: "His bull" is the כהן גדול's bull on יום כפור.

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel disagree.

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: פָּרָה פְּסוּלָה, פָּרוֹ כְּשֵׁרָה.
phrases.english: One said: the heifer is invalid, his bull is valid.
phrases.notes: They're talking about when someone who isn't a כהן does the slaughtering.

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: פָּרוֹ פְּסוּלָה, פָּרָה כְּשֵׁרָה.
phrases.english: And one said: his bull is invalid, the heifer is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: שְׁחִיטַת פָּרָה וּפָרוֹ, רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רבי יצחק's forgotten detail is actually a dispute between רב and שמואל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One אמורא says a זר makes the פרה invalid and the פר valid. The other says the פר is invalid and the פרה valid.

steps.title: Proof that רב is the one who invalidates the פרה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves from another statement that רב holds the פרה is invalid when slaughtered by a זר. He learns this from "אלעזר" and "חוקה."
steps.simpleTranslation: Conclude that it is רב who said the פרה is invalid. רבי זירא said: a פרה slaughtered by a זר is invalid. And רב said about this: we learned "אלעזר" and "חוקה" in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא figures out which אמורא holds which view. It uses a statement where רב explains why a זר may not slaughter the פרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names "אלעזר" the כהן as the one who handles the פרה, so a כהן is required. The word "חוקה" means every detail is required, so leaving it out makes the פרה invalid. Since רב gave this reason, he must be the one who says the פרה is invalid, so שמואל holds the reverse.

keyTerms.meaning: Conclude: a proof that settles who said what
אלעזר the כהן, named in the פרה's פסוקים
"Statute": a sign that every detail is required
About it, commenting on that statement

steps.whyThisMatters: This also answers רבי יצחק's doubt: according to רב, the פרה is the one that is invalid with a זר.

phrases.english: Conclude that it is Rav
who said the heifer is invalid,
for Rabbi Zeira said:
the slaughter of the heifer by a non-priest is invalid,
and Rav said concerning it:
"Elazar" and "statute" we learned regarding it.
phrases.notes: These two words come from the פסוקים in במדבר יט:ב-ג.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּסְתַּיֵּים דְּרַב הוּא דְּאָמַר פָּרָה פְּסוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Determines which side of the dispute in step 6 belongs to רב.
steps.raayaObject: That רב holds a זר makes the פרה invalid.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי זירא's ruling together with רב's comment that "אלעזר" and "חוקה" are written about the פרה.

steps.title: Challenge: the פר also has "אהרן" and "חוקה"
steps.stepSummary: If "אלעזר" and "חוקה" make the פרה need a כהן, then "אהרן" and "חוקה" should make the פר need a כהן too. Yet רב holds the פר is valid with a זר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רב, what is different about the פרה? Because "אלעזר" and "חוקה" are written there? But for his bull, "אהרן" and "חוקה" are written too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב. His own reasoning seems to make the פר invalid with a זר too, which contradicts his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פר's פסוקים name "אהרן" (a כהן) and use the word "חוקה," just like the פרה's. So the same reasoning should apply, and רב's split ruling looks inconsistent.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Asks why two cases are treated differently
אהרן הכהן, named in the פר's פסוקים
Also

phrases.english: And Rav, what is different about the heifer?
That "Elazar" and "statute" are written there?
His bull also:
"Aaron" and "statute" are written there!
phrases.notes: These words come from the פסוקים in ויקרא טז:יא and טז:לד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רב's reasoning from step 7 against his ruling about the פר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a זר may slaughter the פר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same two words that require a כהן for the פרה also appear for the פר.

steps.title: Answer: slaughtering is not an עבודה
steps.stepSummary: The פר is valid with a זר because שחיטה is not counted as a Temple עבודה, so it does not need a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Slaughtering is not an עבודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב. Slaughtering is not one of the special כהן-only services, so a זר may do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "אהרן" and "חוקה" require a כהן only for real עבודות such as sprinkling the blood. Since שחיטה is not an עבודה, those words do not cover it for the פר.

keyTerms.meaning: A Temple service that only a כהן may perform
Not

phrases.english: Slaughtering is not a service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the requirement to real עבודות
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "אהרן" and "חוקה" should require a כהן for every part of the פר, including שחיטה.
steps.terutzMaskana: שחיטה is not an עבודה, so a זר may slaughter the פר.

steps.title: Challenge: then the פרה should also be valid
steps.stepSummary: If שחיטה is not an עבודה, a זר should also be allowed to slaughter the פרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the פרה too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. It seems to prove too much: it should make the פרה valid with a זר as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שחיטה is never an עבודה, then "אלעזר" and "חוקה" should not require a כהן for slaughtering the פרה either. That would undo רב's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: introduces a challenge built on the last answer

phrases.english: If so, the heifer also!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer in step 9 against רב's ruling on the פרה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the פרה is invalid with a זר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If שחיטה is not an עבודה, there is no reason a זר cannot slaughter the פרה.

steps.title: The פרה is different because it is קדשי בדק הבית
steps.stepSummary: The פרה has the status of קדשי בדק הבית, not a regular קרבן, so the rule that שחיטה is not an עבודה does not apply to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פרה is different, because it is קדשי בדק הבית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב. The פרה is a special category, so the usual rule about slaughtering does not apply to it. The next step challenges this answer with a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that שחיטה is not an עבודה belongs to the laws of regular קרבנות. The פרה is holy as קדשי בדק הבית, not as a מזבח offering, so those rules do not carry over. For it, "אלעזר" and "חוקה" require a כהן even for slaughtering.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different: marks something as an exception
Items consecrated for Temple upkeep, not as מזבח offerings

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, a זר may slaughter the פר of the כהן גדול because שחיטה is not an עבודה. A זר may not slaughter the פרה אדומה, because "אלעזר" and "חוקה" require a כהן, and as קדשי בדק הבית the regular קרבן rules do not apply to it. שמואל holds the opposite.
steps.confusionAlert: The פרה is still a holy, Torah-commanded מצוה. Being קדשי בדק הבית just means the usual rules for מזבח offerings do not automatically apply to it.

phrases.english: The heifer is different,
for it is consecrated for Temple maintenance.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי פָּרָה, דְּקׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 10 and settles רב's position.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule that שחיטה is not an עבודה should apply to the פרה too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פרה is קדשי בדק הבית, so regular קרבן rules do not apply, and "אלעזר" and "חוקה" require a כהן even for its שחיטה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב is consistent: the פר is valid with a זר, and the פרה is invalid with a זר.

steps.title: Shouldn't the פרה be valid with a זר all the more so?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב with a קל וחומר: if the פר, a real קרבן, is valid when slaughtered by a זר, then the פרה, which is only קדשי בדק הבית, should certainly be valid with a זר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it all the more so?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 11. If the more holy item (the פר) does not need a כהן to slaughter it, the less holy item (the פרה) surely should not need one either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said the פרה is a different kind of holiness, קדשי בדק הבית, and not a regular קרבן. The גמרא turns that answer against רב: a lower level of holiness should make the rules easier, not stricter. So a זר should be allowed to slaughter it.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so; a קל וחומר argument
A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter one, or the reverse

phrases.english: But isn't it all the more so?
phrases.notes: If the פר, a real קרבן, may be slaughtered by a זר, then surely the פרה, which is only בדק הבית, may be too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 11 by turning the lower holiness of the פרה into a קל וחומר for leniency.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the פרה is invalid when slaughtered by a זר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A lower level of holiness (בדק הבית) should be more lenient than a full קרבן. Since the פר is valid with a זר, the פרה should be valid all the more so.

steps.title: The case of מראות נגעים shows that something that is not an עבודה can still need a כהן
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי answers that the פרה is like מראות נגעים. Examining נגעים is not an עבודה, yet it still requires a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי said: It is just like מראות נגעים, which are not an עבודה and yet require כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שישא knocks down the קל וחומר by pointing to a case where something that is not a Temple עבודה still requires a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר assumed that a כהן is only needed for a real Temple עבודה. נגעים prove this assumption wrong, because only a כהן can declare a נגע pure or impure, even though that is not an עבודה. So the פרה can also need a כהן even though its שחיטה is not an עבודה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is just like; introduces a comparison case
The appearances of צרעת marks, which a כהן must examine
The status of being a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי is not saying that the שחיטה of the פרה is an עבודה. Defending רב's view, he is saying that the פרה needs a כהן even though its שחיטה is not an עבודה, just like נגעים.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Shisha, son of Rav Idi, said:
It is just like the appearances of leprosy marks,
which are not a Temple service,
and yet they require the priesthood.
phrases.notes: So needing a כהן does not depend on something being an עבודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קל וחומר of step 12 with a counterexample.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counterexample that breaks the assumption behind the קל וחומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A כהן is required only for a real Temple עבודה, so the less holy פרה should not need one.
steps.terutzMaskana: The need for a כהן does not depend on something being an עבודה, as נגעים show. The verses ״אלעזר״ and ״חוקה״ require a כהן for the פרה.

steps.title: For שמואל, why do ״אהרן״ and ״חוקה״ disqualify the פר but ״אלעזר״ and ״חוקה״ not disqualify the פרה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to שמואל, who holds that the פר is invalid with a זר because of ״אהרן״ and ״חוקה״. It asks why the same words, ״אלעזר״ and ״חוקה״, do not make the פרה invalid with a זר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to שמואל, who said the פר is invalid: what is different about his פר? That it is written ״אהרן״ and ״חוקה״. With the פרה too, ״אלעזר״ and ״חוקה״ are written!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now examines the opposite opinion, שמואל, and points out what looks like an inconsistency in his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל is the reverse of רב: for him the פר needs a כהן and the פרה does not. But the two cases are described in matching language: a כהן's name plus the word ״חוקה״. If that language disqualifies a זר for the פר, it should do the same for the פרה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different?
His bull, the פר of the כהן גדול on יום כיפור
Statute; a sign that the details are essential

phrases.english: And according to Shmuel, who said his bull is invalid (with a non-priest),
what is different about his bull?
That it is written ״Aaron״ and ״statute״.
With the heifer too,
it is written ״Elazar״ and ״statute״!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִשְׁמוּאֵל, דְּאָמַר פָּרוֹ פְּסוּלָה, מַאי שְׁנָא פָּרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defending רב to examining שמואל, using the same pair of verses discussed in steps 7 and 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that the פרה is valid when slaughtered by a זר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verses for the פר and the פרה are parallel (a כהן's name plus ״חוקה״), so they should lead to the same law.

steps.title: ״לפניו״ shows a זר may slaughter the פרה while אלעזר watches
steps.stepSummary: The פרה is different because the verse says ״וְשָׁחַט אוֹתָהּ לְפָנָיו״: someone slaughters it in front of אלעזר. This implies a זר slaughters and אלעזר watches.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because it is written: ״And he shall slaughter it before him״, meaning that a זר slaughters and אלעזר watches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for שמואל by pointing to a special verse about the פרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the פרה, the Torah says the שחיטה happens ״before him″, meaning before אלעזר. That suggests the slaughterer is someone other than אלעזר. So ״אלעזר״ and ״חוקה״ require a כהן to watch, not to slaughter. The פר has no such verse.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there
Before him, meaning in front of אלעזר
Watches

phrases.english: It is different there,
because it is written: ״And he shall slaughter it before him״,
meaning that a non-priest may slaughter
and Elazar watches.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא against שמואל in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction based on a special verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״אלעזר״ and ״חוקה״ require a כהן to perform the שחיטה of the פרה, just as with the פר.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״לפניו״ shows that a זר slaughters and אלעזר only needs to watch.

steps.title: רב reads ״לפניו״ as a rule not to take attention off the פרה
steps.stepSummary: רב, who requires a כהן to slaughter the פרה, uses ״לפניו״ to teach that the כהן must not take his attention off the פרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב? He reads it as teaching that he must not divert his attention from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question: what does רב do with the verse ״לפניו״, which seemed to allow a זר?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב does not read ״לפניו″ as permission for someone else to slaughter. He reads it as a demand that the כהן keep his full focus on the פרה throughout the process. This way the verse fits with his view that a כהן must do the שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking one's attention off; distraction
That he should not divert his attention

phrases.english: And Rav? (He reads it as teaching) that he must not divert his attention from it.
phrases.notes: The גמרא doesn't say it out loud, but it's asking how רב reads the פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how רב handles the verse that step 15 used for שמואל.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״לפניו″ seems to show that a זר may slaughter the פרה, which goes against רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רב, ״לפניו″ teaches that the כהן must keep his attention on the פרה.

steps.title: Where does שמואל learn the rule against losing focus?
steps.stepSummary: Since שמואל used ״לפניו″ for a זר slaughtering, the גמרא asks where he learns the rule that one must not take attention off the פרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל, from where does he learn that one must not divert his attention?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next step by asking for שמואל's source for the attention rule, since he already used ״לפניו″ for something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that the person handling the פרה must not lose focus. But שמואל already used ״לפניו″ to allow a זר, so he needs a different verse for this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he know it?

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל, שֶׁלֹּא יַסִּיחַ דַּעְתּוֹ מְנָא לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: And Shmuel, from where does he derive that one must not divert his attention?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל, שֶׁלֹּא יַסִּיחַ דַּעְתּוֹ מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for שמואל's source for the attention rule that רב learned from ״לפניו″ in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: שמואל's source for the rule that one must not divert attention from the פרה

steps.title: שמואל learns it from ״לעיניו״ in the burning verse
steps.stepSummary: שמואל learns the attention rule from the verse ״וְשָׂרַף אֶת הַפָּרָה לְעֵינָיו״.
steps.simpleTranslation: He derives it from: ״And he shall burn the heifer in his sight״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives שמואל's source: a different verse about burning the פרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words ״in his sight″ show that the כהן must keep watching and stay focused. So שמואל has a source for the attention rule without using ״לפניו″.

keyTerms.meaning: He derives it
In his sight; before his eyes
And he shall burn

phrases.english: He derives it
from ״And he shall burn the heifer in his sight״.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ: מִ״וְּשָׂרַף אֶת הַפָּרָה לְעֵינָיו״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל learns the attention rule from ״לעיניו״ in the verse about burning.

steps.title: רב needs both verses: one for slaughtering and one for burning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that according to רב both verses are needed: ״לפניו″ teaches the attention rule for the שחיטה, and ״לעיניו″ teaches it for the burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב? One verse is for slaughtering and one is for burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why רב needs ״לפניו″ for the attention rule when ״לעיניו″ already teaches it. Each verse covers a different stage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, the rule about focus must be stated separately for the שחיטה and for the burning. We would not have learned one stage from the other. So neither verse is extra, and רב's reading of ״לפניו″ stands.

keyTerms.meaning: One
Burning

steps.whatToRemember: רב: a כהן must slaughter the פרה, and ״לפניו″ means he must not lose focus during the שחיטה, while ״לעיניו″ means the same for the burning. שמואל: a זר may slaughter the פרה while אלעזר watches (from ״לפניו″), and the attention rule comes from ״לעיניו״ alone.

phrases.english: And Rav? One (verse) is for slaughtering and one is for burning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the implied question of why רב needs ״לפניו״ given that שמואל gets the rule from ״לעיניו״ in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each verse covers a separate stage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״לעיניו״ alone teaches the attention rule, so רב's use of ״לפניו״ would be extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: The attention rule must be taught separately for the שחיטה and for the burning, so רב needs both verses.

steps.title: Why the attention rule must be written for both slaughtering and burning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that neither verse alone would have been enough. Each stage has its own special feature, so we might have limited the rule to that one stage.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both verses are needed. If the Torah had written the rule only about slaughtering, we would say: that is because slaughtering is the start of the service, but burning would not need it. So the Torah had to write it for burning too. And if the Torah had written it only about burning, we would say: that is because the burning is when the פרה actually becomes ready for use, but slaughtering would not need it. So the Torah had to write it for slaughtering too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves רב's claim from the last step: both ״לפניו״ and ״לעיניו״ are needed, and neither one is extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering is special because it is the first act of the service. Burning is special because it is the moment the פרה becomes usable. Since each stage has its own reason to be strict, a verse about only one of them could not be stretched to cover the other.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed: both sources are necessary, and neither is extra
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah or ה׳ as Lawgiver
The start of the service
Becomes fit or ready for use
I would have said no, it does not apply

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the reasons given here are halachic rulings. They are "would-have-thought" reasons, showing why each verse could not be learned from the other.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic צריכותא pattern. Whenever the Torah seems to repeat itself, the גמרא shows that each case had a special feature that would have kept us from learning one case from the other.

phrases.english: And it is necessary (to have both verses)
for if the Merciful One had written it only about slaughtering
(I would say it applies there) because it is the start of the service
but for burning, I would say no (the rule does not apply)
so it is necessary (to write it for burning)
And if the Merciful One had written it only about burning
(I would say it applies there) because now is when the heifer becomes ready for use
but for slaughtering, I would say no
so it is necessary (to write it for slaughtering)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the reasoning behind רב's claim in step 19 that both verses are needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: shows that each verse is needed and is not extra
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought one verse was enough and the other was extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each stage has its own special feature, so the Torah had to state the attention rule for both slaughtering and burning.

steps.title: Which stage is left out of the attention rule?
steps.stepSummary: The Torah wrote the attention rule for only two stages. That suggests some other stage is not included, so the גמרא asks which one it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What stage is this meant to leave out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question that sets up the next move: what does the Torah mean to exclude by writing the rule for only slaughtering and burning?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the Torah named only two stages, those two seem to be the only ones that need constant attention. The גמרא now wants to know which other stage of the פרה process is free of this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, to leave out
What?

phrases.english: To exclude what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 20: if the rule had to be written for these two stages, then other stages are apparently not included.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which stage of the פרה אדומה process does the Torah leave out of the rule about not taking one's attention off the פרה?

steps.title: First suggestion: gathering the ashes and drawing the water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries a first answer. Perhaps the stages left out are gathering the ashes and filling the water for mixing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is meant to leave out gathering its ashes and filling the water for the mixing,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer that begins with ״אילימא״ ("if you say"). It is setting up a suggestion that it will test, and probably reject, in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After burning, the ashes are gathered, and later water is drawn to be mixed with the ashes. These later stages come after the פרה is already ready, so they seem like natural candidates to be left out. The word ״אילימא״ signals that this answer will be challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say: introduces a suggestion that is usually about to be rejected
Gathering its ashes
Filling, or drawing, the water
The mixing of the ashes with the water

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished. ״אילימא״ opens a suggestion, and the גמרא's response to it comes on the next amud. This is not the final answer.

phrases.english: If you say it is to exclude
the gathering of its ashes
and filling the water for the mixing (with the ashes)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first possible answer to the question in step 21, which the גמרא will test next.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A suggested answer: the excluded stages are gathering the ashes and drawing the water for mixing. It is still unresolved on this amud.
